FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.97
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.74
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `scan_health()` marks tools as available whenever the runner function returns without raising, even when the binary is missing or timed out. Evidence: `run_pyright/run_ruff/run_bandit/run_mypy` return `[]` on `"NOT_FOUND"` and also on parse failure; `scan_health()` then unconditionally sets `tools_available[tool_name] = True` inside the `try` block. This makes the health scan report success for tools that never ran.
FOLLOW: The insect-brain-facing health signal becomes silently wrong: missing pyright/ruff/bandit/mypy installations appear healthy rather than unavailable. Downstream, reviewers and any logic consuming `HealthScan.tools_available` will trust empty diagnostics as “no issues” instead of “tool absent / scan failed”. This directly undermines the module’s primary feature “Health scan — static analysis tools between rounds” because the feature can fail dead-silent and still report operational.
PROPOSED_FIX: Change each tool runner to return both diagnostics and an availability/success flag, or minimally have `scan_health()` detect `_run_tool` sentinel failures (`NOT_FOUND`, `TIMEOUT`, empty/invalid output) and set `tools_available[tool_name] = False` for those cases instead of inferring availability from absence of exceptions.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.95
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.79
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` does not sandbox imports or project context; it writes only the patched target file into a temp dir and then runs pyright/ruff/bandit on that isolated basename path. Evidence: `patched_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, os.path.basename(target_path))`; no package tree or sibling modules are copied. For any fix whose file depends on local imports, relative package layout, config, or neighboring modules, the “post-fix” analysis runs in a different environment from the real source tree.
FOLLOW: Fix evaluation can misclassify good fixes as harmful/unevaluable due to broken imports in the sandbox, and bad fixes as safe because cross-file effects are never checked. This crosses the immune pipeline interface: `immune_agents.run_immune_pipeline()` marks findings `verified=True` when endocrine returns SAFE/NEUTRAL. That makes the bug-closed gate fire on corrupted evidence, causing later duplicate findings to be suppressed as “closed” when the fix was never validated against the actual project layout.
PROPOSED_FIX: Sandbox the file within a copied project-relative tree instead of as a lone basename: copy all `source_paths` into the temp dir preserving relative paths, patch the target file inside that mirror, and run tools against the mirrored target from the mirrored project root.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.93
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.71
DESCRIPTION: FIND — test execution in `evaluate_fix()` does not actually validate the patched source. Evidence: the patched file is written into `tmpdir`, but `test_cmd` is executed unchanged with only `cwd=tmpdir`. In the real caller from `immune_agents.py`, `test_cmd` is `["python3", "-m", "pytest", "bench/tests/", ...]`; that path is not copied into `tmpdir`, and no `PYTHONPATH` or rewritten command points tests at the sandbox. The tests therefore either fail for missing files or run against the original checkout rather than the patched sandbox.
FOLLOW: The advertised capability “Fix evaluation — sandbox-test proposed fixes” is effectively dead or misleading. SAFE/HARMFUL verdicts can be assigned without testing the patched code path at all. Because these verdicts feed verification and `verified=True` marking in the immune pipeline, the system can close bugs based on tests that never exercised the candidate fix.
PROPOSED_FIX: Execute tests against a mirrored sandboxed project tree: copy the needed source/test tree into `tmpdir`, rewrite relative test paths to that mirror, and invoke Python with `cwd` at the mirrored repo root so imports and test discovery hit the patched files.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004
SEVERITY: 0.88
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.62
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_compute_fix_verdict()` uses aggregate net change across tools, so regressions in one tool can be canceled by improvements in another and still yield SAFE/NEUTRAL. Evidence: `total_net = net_type_errors + net_ruff_errors + net_bandit_issues`; only `total_net > 0` is harmful. Example: `+3` bandit issues and `-4` ruff issues gives `total_net = -1` and verdict SAFE.
FOLLOW: This produces silently wrong fix safety decisions. Security/type regressions can be hidden by unrelated lint reductions, yet the immune pipeline will mark such fixes verified and suppress future reports via the bug-closed gate. That is high-severity because it corrupts canonical defect state, not just local reporting.
PROPOSED_FIX: Make verdict harmful if any individual net metric is positive; only return SAFE when at least one metric improves and none regress, with tests not failing.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F005
SEVERITY: 0.84
FLAW_CLASS: 4
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58
DESCRIPTION: FIND — the documented health scan capability says endocrine runs `pyright/ruff/bandit` and the module-level constants include `CROSSHAIR_BIN` plus `_CROSSHAIR_TIMEOUT`, but no crosshair runner exists and no crosshair invocation is wired into `scan_health()`. This is dead infrastructure/API drift inside the target file itself.
FOLLOW: One advertised significant feature never fires. Reviewers consuming this module will assume symbolic execution support exists because the binary path, timeout, and `ToolDiagnostic.tool` docstring all mention crosshair. In a PoC focused on “all significant features firing cleanly,” this is misleading dead code and a missing capability in the health scan surface.
PROPOSED_FIX: Either remove crosshair from the endocrine API/docs/constants for now, or add a minimal `run_crosshair()` wired into `scan_health()` so the declared feature actually executes. For PoC speed, the simplest sufficient correction is to remove the unused crosshair claims/constants until implemented.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F006
SEVERITY: 0.79
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.67
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `compute_pacing_signals()` claims `context_budget` is an `int` but contains runtime handling for `dict`, then computes `max(context_budget.values())`. For per-model budgets this is the wrong aggregate for a system-wide `cumulative_context_chars`: it compares cumulative total context against the largest single-model budget. Evidence is the in-function comment plus `if isinstance(context_budget, dict): context_budget = max(...)`.
FOLLOW: Context growth alerts can fail to trigger until the entire system has far exceeded the relevant budget envelope. Since insect_brain uses per-model context budgeting and endocrine is meant to warn on pacing/context pressure, this can suppress the very signal intended to trigger degradation/reset decisions, allowing context overrun to accumulate silently.
PROPOSED_FIX: If a dict is passed, compare cumulative context against the sum of per-model budgets, not the max single-model budget.
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: F007
SEVERITY: 0.73
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.55
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `health_trend()` produces ragged series and drops zeros for absent categories. Evidence: it appends counts only for categories present in each scan: `for cat, count in scan.counts_by_category.items(): trend.setdefault(cat, []).append(count)`. Categories absent in a round get no entry rather than `0`.
FOLLOW: Any downstream trend consumer comparing rounds gets misaligned history lengths and cannot distinguish “category absent this round” from “category not yet seen”. This degrades the stated purpose “for the insect brain to detect worsening/improving code health” because trends are structurally wrong once categories appear or disappear across rounds.
PROPOSED_FIX: Build trends across the union of categories seen in `_scan_history` and append an explicit `0` for categories missing from each scan.
VERIFIED: TRUE
